Title: Regex Tester
Description: Test regular expressions live with the Rust regex engine (WebAssembly): match highlighting, capture and named groups, i/m/s flags and saved patterns.
Keywords: regex tester, regular expression tester, rust regex, regex online, test regex, capture groups, named groups, regex debugger
Instructions: Enter a Rust-flavor regular expression and test string below. Matches will be highlighted.
SaveDialogText: Enter a name for this regular expression pattern.

Seo_Introduction: Write a regular expression and see every match highlighted in your test text as you type, with positions and capture groups listed below. Patterns run on the Rust regex crate compiled to WebAssembly, so syntax and behavior are those of Rust, not of JavaScript.
Seo_DetailedDescription:
Supported syntax includes character classes and Unicode classes such as `\p{Cyrillic}`, greedy and lazy quantifiers, alternation, anchors, word boundaries `\b`, numbered groups, named groups `(?<name>…)` or `(?P<name>…)`, non-capturing groups and inline flags such as `(?i)`. Look-ahead, look-behind and backreferences like `\1` are not supported by this engine — the tool shows the engine's error instead. In exchange, matching time grows linearly with the input, so patterns like `(a+)+$` cannot hang the page.

Flags: **i** ignores case, **m** makes `^` and `$` match at every line, **s** lets `.` match a newline; with **Global** off only the first match is shown. Unicode mode is always on in the Rust engine, so `\w`, `\d` and `.` match non-ASCII letters, digits and characters. Positions are JavaScript string indices (UTF-16, an emoji takes 2). The list shows the first 50 matches, and counting stops at 10,000.

Everything runs locally. A pattern is stored — with its name, flags and sample text, in this browser's localStorage — only when you press **Save Pattern**. Five built-in examples (email, IPv4 address, date, hex color, URL) load with one click.
Seo_Examples:
**Named groups**: `(?<year>\d{4})-(?<month>\d{2})-(?<day>\d{2})` on `Released 2026-10-06, patched 2026-11-02` gives 2 matches; the first is `2026-10-06` at `[9-19]` with year `2026`, month `10`, day `06`.

**Case-insensitive alternation**: `error|warn` with the i flag on the lines `ERROR: disk full` and `Warn: low memory` matches `ERROR` and `Warn`.

**Line anchors**: `^\w+` on the lines `alpha one` and `beta two` matches only `alpha`; with the m flag it matches `alpha` and `beta`.

**Unsupported look-ahead**: `foo(?=bar)` is rejected with “look-around, including look-ahead and look-behind, is not supported” — match `foo(bar)` and use the group instead.
Seo_HowToSteps:
### Step 1: Enter a pattern
Type the expression into **Pattern** without surrounding slashes. **Cheat Sheet** lists the most common tokens.

### Step 2: Set the flags
Under **Flags**, tick **Insensitive**, **Multi-line** or **Dot all** as needed; untick **Global** to see only the first match.

### Step 3: Add test text
Paste text into **Test String** — matches are highlighted as you type.

### Step 4: Inspect the matches
The **Matches** list shows each match with its `[start-end]` position and capture groups.

### Step 5: Save or reuse
Press **Save Pattern** to keep the expression, then **Load** it from **Saved Patterns** or start from one of the **Examples**.
Seo_Tips:
- JavaScript or PCRE patterns that use look-around or `\1` must be rewritten: capture the surrounding text in a group, or check the condition in code.
- `/` needs no escaping, but a literal dot does: write `\.` for “.”.
- Inline flags work inside the pattern too: `(?i)error` is the same as `error` with the i flag.
- Saved patterns live only in this browser; clearing site data deletes them.
- Use `\b` around words (`\bcolou?r\b`) so `colours` is not matched as `colour`.
